sentences.text: The genus Mbiresaurus contains only one known species, Mbiresaurus raathi, which is recognized from a nearly complete skeleton.
Mbiresaurus represents one of Africa's earliest known definitive dinosaurs.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a mostly complete skeleton including a partial skull, jaws, vertebrae, ribs, girdles, and partial limbs.
The Pebbly Arkose Formation also contains fossils of Hyperodapedon, unnamed aetosaurs, herrerasaurids, and synapsids.
Phylogenetic analyses by Griffin et al. (2022) recovered Mbiresaurus as a basal member of Sauropodomorpha.
Mbiresaurus lived during the late Triassic, approximately 231 to 228 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
The time range for Mbiresaurus is the Carnian stage, from 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
